questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted it to be close, so Europe was optimal. I wanted to be in a big city so i could meet other students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The process was very confusing, however the erasmus coordinater at Milan was very sweet and helpfull. 
It was very difficult to find course information at the website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recived assistance through mail, with any question that i had. Otherwise none.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
The teachers did not pay much attention to erasmus students in that sense that exam information were not provided. For example to my first exam, i wrote prior til teacher asking if i should be aware of anything. He said no and that i should relax. However at the exam i needed a culculator and could not get one - he said i should have brought my own. 
In all, just very bad information. Furthermore, in University of Milan there is some kind of rule for writing with a pen or a pencil. This information was not given to us either. Very poor experince with the first exam and midterms.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Milan is very expensive so hard to find a place to a reasonable price. We booked through Airbnb as we were sure that it wasn't a scam. We paid around 16.500kr each month in total (3 people, 5500 each) for an apartment of 43kvm. However, it was in a really great area.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Look in good time. Stay away from the Centrale area - it is dangerous.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Massimo wrote to as about information (name, surname etc) and then he made student cards for us, which we picked up later at an agreed time. 
The course registration were pretty ease.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: we could write to Massimo or the teachers of the course. Little information on the website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: we were 3 people so we always helped eachother. It could be a confusing process, as the registration can change from course to course. However, all in all successfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Always ask the teacher if you are in doubt.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: We had one course on BA level and 2 on MA level. The level were quite nice, and kind of the same as in KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Pretty much the same. However in one course we had role playing, which i never did at KU.
Also we had no papers during the semester which we shoudl turn in.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International business management and accounting
Advanced strategic management 
International Macroeconomics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All good courses. 
in IBMA you should eb aware of role playing - he picks people in the crowd and you are not allowed to say no.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: some erasmus events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: museums!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around Italy by train - ex. Genova, Como (A MUST), Rome, Firenze, Venice etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: learn italian - many italians are bad at english

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: it all

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing in good time, Save up some money or apply for grants in good time (3-4 months before i would recommend), try to learn some italian

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: not being able to speak to people when they did not n´know english. Ex. in the supermarket i always had to find pictures or look up the italian word, if i needed help to find somthing.

questions.answer: Yes
